title: api-client.ts request() sent Content-Type: application/json on a BODYLESS call (autoSchedule's POST, every DELETE) -> Fastify 400s with 'Body cannot be empty when content-type is set to application/json'
detail: Fix: only set Content-Type when init.body !== undefined and is not FormData (`const hasBody = init?.body !== undefined`). Symptom: clicking Auto-schedule in the browser threw that exact string as a banner.

title: api-client.ts request() always parsed the response as JSON, including on 204 No Content (every removeX DELETE) -> the failed parse was read as body?.success being falsy and thrown as ApiError even though res.ok was true
detail: Fix: short-circuit on `res.status === 204` before attempting res.json(), returning undefined without parsing. Symptom: clicking Remove on a staff/shift/roster-assignment row banner-errored 'Request failed with status 204' despite the DELETE having actually succeeded server-side.

title: Coverage grid label read "Required staff vs. scheduled staff" while the cell rendered `${scheduled}/${required}` — the two were inverted, so a manager would read every understaffed hour as overstaffed
detail: Found during the final pre-submission UI pass, once port 3000 was free and the app could be driven in its SHIPPED configuration. coverage-view.tsx line 63 described the grid as 'Required staff vs. scheduled staff, per hour' but line 92 rendered `${cell.scheduled}/${cell.required}`. Verified against real data rather than by reading: Mon 09:00 showed '2/3' where the roster had 2 people on Mon Morning and demand was 39 transactions at N=18, i.e. ceil(39/18)=3 required — so the display is scheduled-first and the label named required first. A non-technical manager following the label reads 2/3 as 'need 2, scheduled 3, comfortably overstaffed' when the truth is the exact opposite, and the cell's red UNDERSTAFFED tint then contradicts their own reading of the numbers. Directly on the brief's graded 'is the UI clear enough for a non-technical manager' criterion. Fixed by rewriting the caption to state the order explicitly ('Each cell reads scheduled / required — the staff booked for that hour over the number the demand calls for') rather than by flipping the render, since the colour badge and every earlier verification session already assume scheduled-first. Lesson: a caption and the value it captions are two independent strings that no test compares — cross-check rendered NUMBERS against the source's template literal, not the caption's prose, and use a cell where the two values differ (a 4/4 cell would have hidden this completely).

title: .gitignore's `coverage/` (meant for Jest/Vitest reports) silently swallowed apps/web/src/app/s/[id]/coverage/ — the Coverage SCREEN, a brief §8 stretch goal, was never committed and the pushed repo had 6 of 7 UI screens
detail: Caught on the final pre-submission pass, and only because that pass ran the app from a FRESH CLONE with `npm run start` (production build) instead of `npm run dev` in the working tree. Symptom chain: /s/:id/coverage returned 404 while the API returned 200 for the same schedule id; the other five tabs all returned 200; .next/server/app/s/[id]/ contained demand, roster, shifts, staff, summary and no coverage directory; `git ls-files apps/web/src/app/s/` listed six page.tsx files, not seven. Root cause: `git check-ignore -v` pointed at .gitignore line 9, `coverage/` — a build-output pattern intended for test coverage reports (jest's coverageDirectory is ../coverage, vitest defaults to coverage/) that matches ANY directory named coverage at ANY depth, including a UI route directory under src/. Every previous verification missed it because they all ran against the local working tree where the file exists; the two earlier fresh-clone tests exercised the API and /roster //summary but never /coverage specifically. Fixed with a scoped negation (`!**/src/**/coverage/`) rather than by renaming the route or narrowing the ignore to `/coverage/`, and verified BOTH directions with git check-ignore: apps/coverage/index.html, apps/web/coverage/lcov.info, packages/scheduling-core/coverage/report.json and coverage/foo.txt all still ignored, while the route file is now trackable. Then swept every .ts/.tsx/.css under apps/*/src and packages/*/src through git check-ignore to confirm coverage was the only casualty (it was). Lessons: (1) a build-output ignore pattern must never be able to match anything under src/ — anchor it or negate src explicitly; (2) `git status` shows nothing for an ignored file, so a missing source file is invisible in the working tree and only appears in a clone; (3) verify a UI from a fresh clone of the PUSHED commit, exercising every route, not from the directory you built it in.

title: Removing a staff member permanently 500-ed the coverage endpoint: soft-delete left their assignments dangling, and FeasibilityGate.eligible THROWS on a staffId missing from SchedulingInput.staff
detail: User reported coverage breaking right after removing staff. Reproduced against the live API and traced it: StaffMember is soft-deleted (deletedAt), so `listByScheduleId` stops returning them, but `RemoveStaffHandler` only called `staff.softDelete` -- their Assignment rows survived untouched. `GetCoverageHandler` rebuilds RosterState by replaying every persisted assignment through `gate.eligible(a.staffId, ...)`, and that method deliberately THROWS on an unknown staffId ('a caller bug, not a feasibility case -- scheduling-core trusts its input completely'). So one removal poisoned the schedule permanently: every later coverage read was a 500, and nothing ever cleaned the rows up. Summary survived because `summarise` skips unknown references instead of throwing, which is why the symptom looked like 'coverage is broken' rather than 'the data is broken'. Fixed in three places, deliberately: (1) `RemoveStaffHandler` now calls a new `assignments.deleteByStaffId` BEFORE the soft delete, (2) `RemoveShiftHandler` got the matching `deleteByShiftId` -- a dangling SHIFT reference never threw (coverage already skipped unresolvable shifts) but silently kept counting toward that person's booked hours, a quieter wrong answer, (3) `GetCoverageHandler` now skips assignments whose staffId is not in `input.staff`, because a READ endpoint must survive data a write path should never have left behind -- and without it every schedule already corrupted by the old bug would have stayed broken after the fix. Verified against the actually-corrupted schedule in the dev DB (500 -> 200) and by re-running the original scenario end to end (delete staff with 5 assignments -> coverage 200, summary 200, 0 rows left behind). Lesson: when a domain function documents that it throws on invalid input because it 'trusts its input', every caller that feeds it PERSISTED data owns that contract -- soft delete quietly breaks it, since the row survives the delete but disappears from the query the caller builds its input from.
